lede: The questions people ask most about the scores, the test costs and individual tasks.

items.a: Besides the design tasks, this challenge has many **rigorous reasoning and algorithm design tasks**, and those are where GPT models are strong. The site lets you change the weights and recompute the scores yourself. **A gap of under three points** can be treated as natural variation.

items.q: Why is 6.1~Sol's score so close to 6~Astra's?
items.a: Because 6.1~Sol is a **top-tier distillation of Astra**: its abilities and behaviour are almost identical.
First, Terra stands on the GPT family's intelligence base. Second, Terra measured **close to 100 TPS**, a real speed edge under a time limit. And this challenge is **not a pure front-end test**.

items.q: Does grading with Opus~5.5 and 6.1~Sol make them favour their own family's models?
items.a: No. I ran dedicated comparisons **graded blind and with model names shown**: when Opus and GPT grade their own family's models, the gap moves by **under 2~points**, which is normal variation. And from the attention mechanism's point of view alone, a grader spends its time checking code and running tests; it does not pay attention to the model's code name.

items.q: How are the test cost and token usage calculated?
a: By an automatic tally that Sol wrote: it adds up the tokens of **the last attempt** from the logs. Subscriptions are priced from ModelDial's weekly quotas, credits at their tier price, and APIs at what was actually paid.

items.q: Why does DeepSeek cost the most?
items.a: DeepSeek runs at **about 200 TPS** and **calls tools very often**, so it reads a great many input tokens.

items.q: Why do Claude and GPT cost so little?
a: Because GPT and Claude subscriptions are **very good value**. API-equivalent cost against the subscription price:
I have paid for both $200 plans for several months, and my own usage matches these numbers. It is a harsh fact, but one we have to face.

items.q: Why did Hy and MiMo score 0?
items.a: Both models **thought furiously for the whole 60~minutes** and never wrote a word: a big fat zero.

items.q: Why does Opus~5.5 score fairly high on all of these?
items.a: Opus has **a very strong drive to design on its own initiative**, and it is fast, which pays off in a timed challenge. That does not prove Opus is always stronger at these tasks when time is open-ended.

items.lead:
If you think a task isn't worth testing,
just **set its weight to 0** on the site.
items.a: Questions about the tasks themselves are **always welcome**.
